en: Buddhagadyaya (*Buddhagajjaya*).
Homage to the Buddha!
1. Homage to Samantabhadra, the eye that perceives the entire field of experience.
Victory, victory to you, O King of Dharma, who are an ocean of the waves of the nectar of compassion, the kinsman of the sun, the bestower of honor and happiness upon your father,
whose conduct is like that of a Buddha, and whose morality is utterly pure!

3. O you whose web of rays is radiant, who possess various kinds of divine power, who have cast away all faults in the world, and whose excellent appearance is saluted [by all]; 4. O you adorned with beautiful liberation, who speak the distinguished Magadhi language.
O subduer of the great Māra, you who have shattered the burden of existence;
O Lord of wise men, adorned with auspicious verses, whose footsteps are honored, and who has accumulated a mass of benefit.
6. O you who lie upon the best of lion-thrones, whose eyes resemble the lotus, who bring happiness to the people of the world, and whose feet are bowed to by the restless gods;
7. O you who are most skillful in conquering Time, the sun to the mountain of Dharma.
You who remove the evil intellects of foolish people; you who subdued Āḷavaka;
you who are worthy of worship by gods and men; you who possess the heroic power to awaken the wise;
you whose activity is the accomplishment of the welfare of others; you who are the Teacher of the governance of the three worlds.

9. Seated upon the lotus-throne of the water of the Dānavas, seated upon the wise and pure variegated throne, seated upon the Rudrāsana free from delusion, seated upon the vajra-throne at the foot of the Bodhi tree;
10. Knower of the qualities of the Lord of Sacrifice who is bowed to by all, possessor of supreme wisdom, clearly manifest as the support of discernment.

O Knower of how to strike the forces of the enemy that is ignorance, O Great One possessing the foundation of wisdom and the six supernormal knowledges; O You whose arrow is the essence consisting of intellect, O Destroyer of the causes of those distressed by calamity,
O Bestower of the glory of agelessness and immortality, O Leader of the world of the moving and the unmoving.
12. O you whose soft speech is heard afar; O you who have obtained the divine worship of the gods; O you who delight the people through your excellent hearing;
O you who bring joy to the noble family of Māyā; O you who are renowned throughout the world. 13.
O you who have abandoned anger even toward those who have harmed or destroyed what is dear; O you who are satisfied with the most excellent things and free from all evil.
O one who has conquered the afflictions of the learned and the distinguished; whose form is characterized by the fourfold set of eight [qualities];
whose boundaries are drawn by the calculation of the states of the worthy; O delightful one who gladdens people by bestowing good fortune;
O one who has dried up desire with the mere fragments of your words; O moon to the ocean of the Śākya royal lineage.

15. You whose vast policy of inspired teaching has been established, whose root is the captivating essence of awakening, who have warded off the amorous play of the women of Māra, and who have fulfilled the ten perfections and moral conducts;
16. You who are the sun with the radiant light of the dawn of desire, whose regions shine with a golden luster.

O you whose priceless hair is filled with a dark radiance, O you who possess the light that illuminates a fathom-wide halo; O moon of the perfected power of yoga and all-encompassing knowledge, O full moon of the lower lip, O full moon of the perfected half-moon [of the Dharma], O wise one renowned for the fullness of the scriptures, O half-moon of the youthful brilliance of the *ūrṇā* hair-tuft.
18. O King who is the lord of the world, rising like a jar; O King praised by the wielder of the thunderbolt (Indra);
O King of virtuous deeds resembling the ocean; O King of the true Dharma, the Lord of Speech (Brahmā) dwelling in the ocean of Śambhu.
19. O Buddha who has destroyed all the evils arising from the thickets of existence; O one who is pure in conduct and other virtues, through the immersion in ever-shining qualities.

Accomplished in the splendor and beauty of the various manifestations of Viriñca’s radiance, followed by a soaring garland of great banners; speaking with the essence of auspiciousness at every moment, bearer of incomparable qualities, free from all terrors, you who have utterly cleansed the stains of worldly passion and anger, adorned with the ornament of immeasurable and supreme ethical discipline.

21. O you who are impelled, dispatched, procreative, moving, renowned, virtuous, joyful, blossoming, abundant in those who bow before you, whose power is manifest, whose love is evident, and who are exceedingly mighty;
22. O deliverer, world-renowned refuge for all people, destroyer of enemies, and bringer of auspiciousness to the host of the brave and the faithful.
O Teacher, whose hands and feet are perfected through the abandonment of enemies and truth; O you who spread the rays of excellent light in six distinct colors;
O bee of honeyed devotion toward the company of virtuous people arranged in manifest order;
O you who possess devotion on the battlefield of the destruction of saṃsāra; O lofty sage, who rejoices in the auspiciousness of the city of liberation!
24. You have composed a tantra that destroys the fear of worldly existence;
you have mastered many kinds of tantras taught by the wise; your mantra of nine qualities is renowned throughout the three worlds. 25.
Your roar is the supreme sound to be proclaimed amidst the tumultuous clamor; you are the supreme service to those worthy of honor for their virtues and character.
O Supreme God, the sole object of affection for the world, who transcends all states of existence that are pleasant yet subject to ripening;
O you whose splendor awakens the truth like the sun, the moon, and fire; O you who destroy the darkness of the lineage of transmigratory existence through the heat of your penance and the truth;
O you who establish the truth through words of immeasurable virtue; O you who awaken the four truths for the welfare of all beings.
27. You who crush the wheel of the playful sport of the surface of the earth through its lack of movement; you who increase the wheel of many meritorious deeds that lead to happy rebirths;
you who shatter the wheel of karma that consists of existence within the realms of evil destinies; you who have set in motion the excellent wheel of Dharma for the sake of the world. 28.

You who have clearly explained the ripening [of karma] through the realization of the true nature of the perfected scriptures; you who have made known the celestial realm by proclaiming the tradition of the Buddhas.

One whose sorrow has been extinguished by the expansion of pure lineage; one who has made the world aware through the spreading of the attainment of supernatural powers (ṛddhi); one whose golden body has lost its luster because it serves as a vessel for food and drink made of clay and earth;
one who has deceived the wicked by means of a multitude of festivals and charming, variegated births; and one whose footprints are marked upon the peaks and summits of the entire earth.
30. O you whose conduct is celebrated in song, who have cast away all affliction; O abode of the principles of the immeasurable and stainless Dharma-discipline;
O you whose teeth are beautiful like a necklace of many white jewels; O you whose face is as lovely as the orb of the cool-rayed moon. 31.
O you who gladdened Grandfather Brahmā on the day of your birth; O you who bring about pure merit for the benefit of the world free from stain.

O you whose feet are lotuses beyond the range of Rāhu’s eyes, who are the fierce battle of the strength of arms against the many heroic Māras; O you whose speech is the essence of abundant moonlight, the very limit of the mass of love; O destroyer of the names and forms of Bhīma, Bhāva, Bhāma, and Rāga;
O Vāmadeva, who obstructs the path to the feet of Kāmanātha with your melodies; O you who are beautiful with a name and form that are the abode of heaps of gold.

33. You are the one who shatters the mass of evil views flashing forth in debate; you are the one who brings about the destruction of the mass of delusive proliferation arising from the mind; you are the one whose lotus feet are frequented by a multitude of blossoming lotuses; you are the one who has broken the mass of [false] distinctions by means of the intellect perfected through the Vedas. 34. You are worshipped by the entire world; you have dispelled all sorrows; you are the liberator from the association with the origin of all suffering and pain.

O you whose speech is sweet, essential, cool, manifest, and sublime; O you whose lotus-eye is expanded and adorned by a mass of rays that reach all objects of perception without exception; O you whose lotus-face shines with ever-new grace, dispelling all impurity; O you whose lotus-feet, beloved by the entire world, resound of their own accord at the time of your departure.
36. O Tathāgata who is eternally graceful, eternally generous, eternally compassionate; O Tathāgata who is eternally radiant, eternally teaching, and eternally existent;

O Tathāgata who is eternally marvelous, eternally affectionate, and eternally joyful; O Tathāgata who is eternally auspicious, eternally beautiful, and eternally worthy of worship. 37. O You whose pair of feet arose from the most excellent water-born [lotus] that moves with the threefold purity; O You who have restrained the throats of various humans through the discipline that removes manifold evils.
O Lord whose pair of feet is set with jewels from the crowns of gods bowing down, who have shattered the prison-chains of worldly existence filled with the burden of many objects of sense;

O illuminator of the path of the primary scriptures that gently sways the root of people’s conduct; O forest of the teaching that destroys the auspicious play of Śiva, which is like the deadly *hālāhala* poison;

O mass of clouds bearing the weapon of the crescent moon, which removes the dense thicket of the minds of young women; O destroyer of the pride and impetuosity of the black-bodied elephant on Mount Nāla, who causes a great clamor.

39. Whose exceedingly sweet and clear voice delights the forest; whose soft feet are like lotuses situated in the hearts of people; who shatters the multitude of sins through the power of discipline; and whose delight is the incessant bestowing of the true Dharma. 40. Whose entire realm is rendered stainless by the tenfold power of the intellect from the soles of his reddish feet; and who constantly purifies the great earth with the surrounding waves of the ocean of compassion.

With palms as soft as lotuses blossomed by the rays of the clear-splendid sun, and with the fragrance exhaled from the mouths of the most excellent and fragrant hosts of deities gathered from the ten directions—
41. Whoever respectfully writes or recites this faultless and exceedingly charming prose of Dharmarāja, or whoever hears it,
shall attain and eternally experience all enjoyments within the abodes of the three worlds, culminating in the bliss of peaceful Nirvāṇa.
May there be success. May there be auspiciousness. For the sake of the prose composition on the Buddha.
